plan: [ In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. With value $30, bidding 30 ensures we win exactly when the highest competing bid is below 30, paying that second-highest price, yielding nonnegative profit. There’s no prior-round info to adjust strategy. Bids are in $0.1 increments, so 30.0 is valid. ]

[ In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: your bid affects only whether you win, not the price you pay (which is the second-highest bid). Overbidding risks winning at a price above your value; underbidding risks losing when you should profit. With value $7 and no informative history (one round, values i.i.d. uniform 0–49), the optimal bid is exactly 7. This maximizes expected profit and avoids negative payoffs. ]

[ In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value: your bid only affects whether you win, not the price you pay (which is the second-highest bid). With uniform values and no exploitable history in a single round, shading risks losing profitable wins; overbidding risks negative surplus if second-highest exceeds your value. Therefore, to maximize expected profit, bid exactly your value: 36.0. ]
